questions.title: ValidationError fieldErrors type: single vs array
questions.context: Base_System.md §2.2 defines fieldErrors as Record<string, string> (single message per field). But Phase 4's CommandValidationError has fieldErrors: Record<string, string[]>. Which should PresentationError use?

options.label: Record<string, string> (single message per field)
options.description: Matches Base_System.md spec exactly. Simpler for UI rendering. Breaks consistency with Application layer's array type.

options.label: Record<string, string[]> (multiple messages per field)
options.description: Matches Application layer's CommandValidationError. Richer validation feedback. UI needs to handle arrays.

questions.title: SystemError.severity: string union vs Kernel Severity enum
questions.context: Base_System.md defines severity as 'warning'|'error'|'critical' (string union). Kernel has a Severity enum with same values. Enum values don't survive JSON round-trip reliably across RSC.

options.label: Plain string union: 'warning' | 'error' | 'critical'
options.description: 100% serialization-safe. Matches Base_System.md spec. No Kernel Severity enum needed.

options.label: Template literal from Severity enum
options.description: Type-level alignment with Kernel. At runtime still plain strings. Slightly more complex type.

questions.title: NotFoundError: optional vs required suggestedAction
questions.context: Base_System.md shows suggestedAction?: string. Optional keeps flexibility but means client must handle undefined every match.

options.label: Optional (suggestedAction?: string)
options.description: Matches spec. Flexible. Client must handle missing action.

options.label: Required (suggestedAction: string)
options.description: Always provides action. Simpler client. May force 'Go back' as default.

questions.title: AuthorizationError.requiredPermission: keep or drop?
questions.context: requiredPermission?: string leaks internal permission names to the client. Enables granular 'you need X permission' messages.

options.label: Keep as optional (requiredPermission?: string)
options.description: Enables detailed UI messages. Permissions typically not sensitive.

options.label: Drop — use userMessage only
options.description: Security-first: never expose permission structure. UserMessage conveys access denial.

questions.title: PresentationResult metadata: include or omit in v1?
questions.context: Base_System.md §3.2 defines metadata with operationId, duration, timestamp for Success; operationId, timestamp, retryAfter for Failure. Requires Server Action instrumentation.

options.label: Include metadata (match spec exactly)
options.description: Richer client observability. Enables retry-after UX. More mapper code.

options.label: Omit metadata in v1 — minimal DU only
options.description: Simpler types, less code. Add in follow-up phase.

options.label: Partial: only operationId on both variants
options.description: Minimal useful metadata for correlation. Middle ground.

questions.title: operationId type: string vs branded OperationId
questions.context: Kernel has branded OperationId type. Branded types survive JSON as strings. But DUs should be plain serializable.

options.label: Plain string in DU
options.description: DU stays 100% plain. Clean separation: brands for server, strings for transport.

options.label: Reuse branded OperationId
options.description: Keeps type safety. At runtime it's a string. But creates dependency on Kernel branded type.

questions.title: Error variant detection: how does mapper choose the right variant?
questions.context: ApplicationError has specific subclasses (UseCaseExecutionError, AuthorizationFailedError, CommandValidationError). Mapper must decide which PresentationError variant to produce.

options.label: Duck-type on properties (fieldErrors, reason, code)
options.description: No class imports needed. Works with any ApplicationError. Matches prior duck-typing pattern.

options.label: Exhaustive instanceof check
options.description: Precise — no false matches. Couples to every specific error class.

options.label: Hybrid: instanceof for known, duck-type fallback
options.description: Most robust. Check known classes first, fallback to properties for unknown.

questions.title: Unexpected ApplicationError: fallback variant?
questions.context: Mapper cannot anticipate every ApplicationError. What happens with unknown/novel error types?

options.label: Map to SystemError (catch-all)
options.description: Safe fallback. User sees 'Something went wrong' with error code.

options.label: Log and return generic result
options.description: Pure safety: never return unexpected structure. May lose error context.

options.label: Let mapper throw — caught by error boundary
options.description: Forces handling new error types. Risk of production crashes.

questions.title: User message strategy: auto-generate or manual mapping?
questions.context: PresentationError needs user-friendly messages. Options: pass through ApplicationError message with sanitization, or require explicit mappings.

options.label: Auto-generate from ApplicationError message
options.description: Simpler mapper. Requires messages to be user-friendly.

options.label: Require explicit userMessage mapping
options.description: Ensures user-friendly output. May need message registry later.

options.label: Hybrid: auto-generate default + override param
options.description: Default to sanitized message. Allow per-code overrides.

questions.title: Factory functions for PresentationError variants?
questions.context: DUs have no constructors. Options: standalone factories (like ok()/err()), single createPresentationError(), or inline object literals.

options.label: Standalone factories per variant
options.description: E.g., createValidationError(fieldErrors). Type-safe, tree-shakeable. Follows ok()/err() pattern.

options.label: Single factory with discriminated input
options.description: createPresentationError({ type: 'Validation', ... }). One import. More complex signature.

options.label: No factories — inline object literals
options.description: Zero extra code. Repetitive — every Server Action writes { _tag: 'ValidationError', ... }.

questions.title: Type narrowing helpers: isSuccess, isFailure, match helper?
questions.context: TypeScript narrowing on _tag already works. Extra helpers add convenience but more code. Client-side pattern.

options.label: None — native narrowing sufficient
options.description: if (result._tag === 'Success') works perfectly. Zero extra code.

options.label: isSuccess / isFailure guards only
options.description: Convenience guards. Minimal code. Common pattern (c.f. React Query).

options.label: Full match() function for client
options.description: result.match({ onSuccess, onFailure }). Follows monadic pattern. Adds function to pure DUs.

questions.title: Scaffold stub files: which to DELETE vs RETAIN?
questions.context: Phase 6 has OOP-style scaffold stubs. Phase 4 D-12 and Phase 5 D-15 establish deletion pattern for type alias stubs. Specific/ has nested category subdirectories needing flattening.

options.label: Aggressive cleanup — delete all OOP stubs, flatten Specific/
options.description: Follow Phase 4/5 pattern. DELETE: presentation-error.contract.ts/validator.ts/type-guard.ts, all presentation-result.* stubs except .ts. Flatten Specific/ subdirectories.

options.label: Selective — keep type-guards as runtime DU validators
options.description: RETAIN type-guard files as runtime isPresentationError() checks. Delete contract/validator stubs. Flatten Specific/.

options.label: Minimal — keep stubs, flatten later
options.description: Delete only clear contradictions (contract files). Keep type-guard/validator stubs empty. Keep Specific/ subdirectories.

questions.title: NetworkError variant: should it carry statusCode or retryAfter?
questions.context: Base_System.md defines NetworkError as just { userMessage, retryable }. No status code, no retryAfter. HTTP errors have status codes (429=rate limit, 503=unavailable) that the client could use. Timeouts vs 404s vs 503s all become the same variant.

options.label: Keep minimal: userMessage + retryable only
options.description: Matches spec. Simple type. Client can't differentiate error subtypes. No status code leakage.

options.label: Add statusCode?: number
options.description: Enables HTTP-aware error handling. Optional for generic errors.

options.label: Add statusCode + retryAfter?: number (seconds)
options.description: Full HTTP semantics. Enables 'retry after X seconds' countdown UI.

questions.title: ValidationError vs NotFoundError boundary in mapper
questions.context: When a user submits an entity ID that doesn't exist, is it ValidationError or NotFoundError? The Application layer wraps both as AppError subclasses, but the Presentation mapper must choose one variant.

options.label: NotFoundError by error code prefix (NOT_FOUND_*)
options.description: Errors starting with NOT_FOUND → NotFoundError. Others → ValidationError. Clean prefix convention.

options.label: NotFoundError only for explicit 404 semantics
options.description: Only AuthorizationFailedError → AuthorizationError, CommandValidationError → ValidationError. Everything else → SystemError.

options.label: Merge: ValidationError covers 'invalid input' and 'not found'
options.description: One 'input error' path on client. suggestedAction or fieldErrors disambiguate.

questions.title: Single unified mapper vs two separate mappers?
questions.context: Scaffold has two files (error mapper + result mapper). But the real entry point is ApplicationResult<T> (OOP monad). The mapper must unwrap isSuccess/isFailure, extract data/error, map to DU.

options.label: Single: toPresentationResult<T>(appResult, params?)
options.description: One function handles both paths. Internal delegation. Single import for Server Actions.

options.label: Two: error mapper (AppError→PresError) + result wrapper
options.description: Separate concerns. Error mapping testable in isolation.

options.label: Keep both scaffold files with restructured responsibility
options.description: Error mapper: AppError→PresError. Result mapper: AppResult→PresResult (calls error mapper).

questions.title: Mapper error handling: what if mapper itself throws?
questions.context: The mapper is safety-critical — last transform before RSC boundary. Prior phase mappers are server-to-server and can throw. This one can't crash the client.

options.label: Try/catch wrapper → generic SystemError on throw
options.description: Never throws. On error: log + return SystemError with PRES_MAPPER_ERROR code.

options.label: Assertive: let it throw — error boundary catches
options.description: Simpler code. But loses error type — boundary can't distinguish mapper crash from business error.

options.label: Hybrid: try/catch in result mapper, assertive in error mapper
options.description: Result mapper guarantees never-throw. Error mapper is pure logic, throws on impossible states.

questions.title: Should all PresentationError variants carry errorCode?
questions.context: Only SystemError has errorCode. Without codes on other variants, client error monitoring can't distinguish e.g., 'ValidationError: email invalid' from 'ValidationError: password too short'.

options.label: Add errorCode to ALL 5 variants
options.description: Uniform traceability for every variant. Slightly more verbose but complete.

options.label: Keep errorCode on SystemError only
options.description: Matches spec. userMessage suffices for UI. Simpler types.

options.label: Add to AuthorizationError + NetworkError too
options.description: Middle ground: codes where subtype matters most. ValidationError/NotFoundError are self-describing.

questions.title: Specific/ directory: one file per variant vs single DU type file?
questions.context: Scaffold has 3 subdirectories (Validation-Ui-Errors, Network-Ui-Errors, System-Ui-Errors) with empty files. No Authorization or NotFound files. DUs are a single type — splitting 5 variants across files means 5 imports.

options.label: Single file: presentation-error.types.ts in Errors/ root
options.description: All 5 variants + PresentationError union in one file. Single import. Specific/ deleted.

options.label: Flatten Specific/: one file per variant
options.description: Delete subdirectories. Flat files: validation-error.type.ts, etc. Specific/index.ts barrel.

options.label: Keep subdirectories, add Authorization + NotFound
options.description: Retain structure. Add missing directories. Inconsistent with Phase 3-5 flattening.
